newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Family of dead Cypriot files suit against Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Family of dead Cypriot files suit against Turkey.

text.p: The family of a Greek Cypriot killed in violent clashes on divided Cyprus last year have applied to the European Commission of Human Rights to find Turkey guilty of human rights abuses, their lawyer said on Saturday.
"The suit was based on the deprivation of human life without reason or cause and in that horrible manner that we and all of mankind witnessed," lawyer George Papacharalambous told Cyprus radio.

Tassos Isaak, 24, was clubbed to death with bats and steel bars by a group of Turks in a United Nations-controlled buffer zone during violent clashes in the southeastern village of Dherinia on August 11.
His death was broadcast live by television stations.

Isaak, a waiter, had been taking part in a demonstration organised by Greek Cypriot motorcyclists against the division of the island, virtually partitioned since Turkish troops occupied its north in 1974.
People from the Turkish-held areas of the island held a counter-demonstration in the same area at the same time.
"I don't believe we will have any difficulties because this is a clear-cut case," Papacharalambous said.
Three days later his cousin, Solomos Solomou, 26, was shot and killed by Turkish forces when he attempted to crawl up a flagpole in the same area to remove a Turkish flag hours after Isaak's funeral.
Cyprus has been divided since Turkey invaded the northern third of the island in 1974 in the wake of a brief Greek Cypriot coup engineered by the military ruling Greece at the time.
